title: Transit Gateway route mismatch investigation
content:
Summary:

Quick personal notes while debugging egress failures for a customer-private stack routed via AWS Transit Gateway (TGW) -> on-prem -> internet. Intermittent TLS handshake failures and long tail latency for outbound model downloads (S3 signed URLs) observed. Symptoms only visible when traffic egresses through the peering/TGW path; direct-hosted tests work fine.

Symptoms observed: 
- Sporadic TLS handshake error from model fetcher: "SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, errno=104" and occasional "unexpected EOF".
- Repeated 502/524 style timeouts from edge proxy when upstream is on-prem NAT path.
- Wide variance in RTTs; some requests show 10-50ms, others 700-1200ms before TLS abort.
- Packet captures show bursts of retransmits then an outright RST or connection reset on the same flows that later succeed.
- Smaller payloads OK; larger object downloads fail more often.

Timeline (quick):
- 2025-08-09 initial customer report (high error rate on private deploys).
- 2025-08-10 reproduced in lab with WG tunnel and TGW attachment.
- 2025-08-11 confirmed path difference: direct internet egress (NAT GW in same AZ) is stable. TGW->onprem egress exhibits failures.
- 2025-08-15 tested MTU/MSS adjustments and transient fix observed.
- 2025-08-19 ran conntrack/ss + long tcpdump -> found SYN+ACK retransmit pattern and occasional path MTU drops.

Commands I ran (notes to self: copy/paste snippets into runbook later):
- Trace and DNS checks:
  dig @10.0.0.2 +short example.s3.amazonaws.com
  dig +trace example.s3.amazonaws.com
  host -t A example.private.ourdomain.com  -- to validate split-horizon

- Path checks:
  traceroute -n -T -p 443 <onprem-egress-ip>
  mtr --tcp --port 443 <onprem-egress-ip>
  tcptraceroute <onprem-egress-ip> 443

- Packet captures (from pod host / bastion):
  sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/tgw-egress.pcap host <onprem-egress-ip> and port 443
  sudo tcpdump -i wg0 -nnn -s 0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0'

- Socket / kernel checks:
  ss -tanp | grep <upstream-ip>
  sudo conntrack -L | grep <upstream-ip>
  sudo sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 (toggled during test)

- Application level repro:
  curl -v --connect-timeout 5 --retry 3 --max-time 30 "https://example.s3.amazonaws.com/large-obj" --resolve example.s3.amazonaws.com:<port>:<onprem-egress-ip>
  openssl s_client -connect <onprem-egress-ip>:443 -tlsextdebug -msg

Observed outputs / helpful snippets: 
- curl trace (repeated failures):
  * TCP_NODELAY set
  * Connected to <onprem-egress-ip> (10.5.12.34) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS 1.3 (IN), Certificate (0), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
  * recv cleanup: Connection reset by peer
  * curl: (56) OpenSSL SSL_read: Connection was reset, errno 104

- tcpdump timeline excerpt (simplified):
  10:12:01.234567 IP pod -> onprem SYN
  10:12:01.234876 IP onprem -> pod SYN,ACK
  10:12:01.334999 IP pod -> onprem ACK
  10:12:02.500123 IP pod -> onprem PSH, ACK (first data)
  10:12:02.700456 IP onprem -> pod RST
  repeated flow, next attempt succeeds after MSS clamp changed

- conntrack shows large number of ESTABLISHED entries and a few TIME_WAITs for the same 5-tuple; under stress we saw conntrack table near threshold.

What I tried and results: 
1) Lowering MTU on WireGuard tunnel from 1420 -> 1360 (mss clamping on iptables) -> immediate reduction in failure rate for larger objects. Smaller objects were never impacted.
   - Related: confirmed PMTU discovery seemed to be failing across the on-prem link; ICMP blackhole suspected.
2) Enabled net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on the node -> improved path learning for some flows, reduced retransmits.
3) Temporarily increased conntrack table size on on-prem NAT box -> fewer mid-flight resets during connection spikes.
4) Reproduced TLS failure with openssl s_client; sometimes server sends TCP RST before handshake completes.
5) Tested AWS side: verified TGW propagation table and route table association. Found one stale route in an AZ attachment that pointed to a deprecated transit VPC — likely routing asymmetric path for some subnets. Removed the stale route and re-tested -> marginal improvement but not complete resolution.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Path MTU / ICMP blackholing causing segmented TCP segments to be dropped; larger payloads fail. Supported by MSS/MTU fixes.
B) Asymmetric routing via stale TGW route causes packets to traverse a middlebox that drops or modifies TCP options (SACK, timestamps) leading to handshake/stream issues. Supported by stale route discovery.
C) Conntrack exhaustion / aggressive NAT timeout on on-prem NAT causing mid-connection resets under bursty workload. Supported by conntrack near-threshold.
D) Middlebox (firewall/proxy) performing TLS inspection or resetting initial client hello for large handshake sizes (client certs / SNI ext). Evidence weaker but seen RSTs timed right after client hello.

Repro recipe for lab: 
1) Setup WG tunnel from test host -> onprem NAT (mirror topology).
2) Attach VPC to TGW, configure route to point to onprem NAT.
3) From pod, curl large S3 object with --resolve to force the onprem egress IP.
4) Simultaneously run tcpdump on both sides and monitor conntrack.
5) Tweak MTU/MSS/clamp and tcp_mtu_probing to observe changes.

Temporary mitigations applied so far: 
- Set mtu 1360 on wg0 for affected nodes cluster-wide (managed via daemonset) as a quick mitigation. Reduced error-rate by ~85% for reported customer traffic.
- Increased conntrack max on on-prem NAT per infra team's guidance.
- Removed stale TGW route (still monitoring for regressions).

Next steps / TODOs: 
- Coordinate with on-prem network team to inspect firewall box for TCP option mangling / TLS resets.
- Run controlled PMTU probing (iperf with -M MSS) across production path to confirm blackhole.
- Add passive instrumentation: collect SNI + TLS version + error code for failed fetch attempts (masked / truncated where necessary for privacy).
- Add automated test in CI that simulates TGW egress > 1MB object download to catch regressions.
- If MTU mitigation persists, document as part of private-deploy runbook (include daemonset change, rollback steps).

Notes / random findings: 
- Observed that when client attempted TLS 1.3 with large hello (many ALPNs + SNI + cert types) the packets were slightly larger than MSS and were the ones dropped. Smaller hello (curl -k with reduced ALPN) often passed.
- AWS side: checked TGW route propagation logs (flow logs) and saw a few samples of asymmetric return paths.
- Consider adding an enforcement of MSS clamp in egress path as long-term remedy.

Short-term conclusion: most likely a PMTU/MTU + asymmetric routing interplay. The MTU tweak + conntrack increase fixed bulk of user-visible errors, but still want to eliminate root cause (ICMP blackhole or middlebox).

If I forget later: re-run the failed curl test with --trace-time and include hex dump (-v --trace-ascii) then attach pcap.

End of scratchpad (messy). Will tidy for runbook once we confirm on-prem firewall behavior.
